# Avoid redundant dictionary lookups when diffing keyed items

Hash each old-tree `@key` once when building the keyed-item diff lookup

## Description

When a sibling range contains `@key`ed elements or components, `RenderTreeDiffBuilder.BuildKeyToInfoLookup` builds a `Dictionary<object, KeyedItemInfo>`. For each old-tree key it called `ContainsKey` and then the indexer setter, which is two hash lookups. Keys are `object`, so each lookup costs a virtual `GetHashCode`/`Equals`.

This change uses a single `TryAdd` for old-tree keys. The new-tree pass is unchanged and still uses `TryGetValue` followed by the indexer. Duplicate-key detection, the exceptions it throws, and the diff output all stay the same. There are no public API or behavior changes.

> **Update:** An earlier revision also used `CollectionsMarshal.GetValueRefOrAddDefault` in the new-tree pass. That part was removed (95837ac8) to comply with a project rule against `CollectionsMarshal`, `MemoryMarshal`, `Unsafe` and `stackalloc` in these perf changes. Most of the earlier ~8–10% win came from that part. The remaining win is small (~3%), close to the noise on this VM.

### Benchmark

The PR adds `KeyedListDiffBenchmark` in `src/Components/Components/perf`. It diffs a `<ul>` with 500 `@key`ed `<li>` items, once in the same order and once with a swap, an insert and a removal. Setup: BenchmarkDotNet `--config perflab` (InProcess) on a 2 vCPU Linux VM, 6 interleaved A/B rounds. Both versions allocate 0 B.

| Method | main (median of 6) | PR (median of 6) | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ComputeDiff_KeyedList_SameOrder | 29.80 µs | 28.55 µs | ~−4% |
| ComputeDiff_KeyedList_Reordered | 29.88 µs | 29.03 µs | ~−3% |

### Tests

- `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Tests`: 1303 passed, 8 skipped. This includes the `RenderTreeDiffBuilderTest` keyed and duplicate-key cases.

### Benchmark (3 interleaved rounds)

`KeyedListDiffBenchmark` (added in this PR), 500 `@key`ed items.

| Round | Benchmark | main Mean | PR Mean | Δ time | main Allocated | PR Allocated |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | ComputeDiff_KeyedList_SameOrder [ItemCount=500] | 30.06 µs | 28.33 µs | -5.8% | 0 B | 0 B |
| 1 | ComputeDiff_KeyedList_Reordered [ItemCount=500] | 29.96 µs | 28.98 µs | -3.3% | 0 B | 0 B |
| 2 | ComputeDiff_KeyedList_SameOrder [ItemCount=500] | 29.13 µs | 29.67 µs | +1.9% | 0 B | 0 B |
| 2 | ComputeDiff_KeyedList_Reordered [ItemCount=500] | 29.74 µs | 28.58 µs | -3.9% | 0 B | 0 B |
| 3 | ComputeDiff_KeyedList_SameOrder [ItemCount=500] | 30.10 µs | 29.44 µs | -2.2% | 0 B | 0 B |
| 3 | ComputeDiff_KeyedList_Reordered [ItemCount=500] | 30.23 µs | 32.77 µs | +8.4% | 0 B | 0 B |

Result: **within noise**. `SameOrder` measured −5.8%, +1.9% and −2.2%, and `Reordered` measured −3.3%, −3.9% and +8.4%. Neither version allocates. In this 3-round A/B I can't separate the remaining change from noise.

Setup: BenchmarkDotNet v0.13.0 `--config perflab` (InProcess, MemoryDiagnoser, 3 warmup + 15 measured iterations); AMD EPYC 9V74, 2 vCPU, Ubuntu 24.04 container; .NET SDK 12.0.100-alpha.1.26521.103, .NET 12.0.0 runtime (X64 RyuJIT). `main` is the PR's merge base `4f556f73a6`. `PR` is the same tree with only this PR's `src/**/src` changes applied. Both builds use the same benchmark source. Run order: main, PR, main, PR, main, PR.

**🤖 Posted by ASP.NET Core Perf 2 (AI Agent)**
